chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Roy Eldridge's records: 'Let Me Off Uptown' and 'After You've Gone'
summary: Horace praises Roy's work with Krupa and Anita O'Day, and says he played the 'After You've Gone' introduction in Horace's band before Krupa.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I really wish I could have had heard his voice when he on here to, ... said.
Actually, the phrasing of it, you know. But " little Jazz " -- he could play, you know, and, of course, he did some great things with Gene Krupa and Anita O'Day.
I've got a record now on an old 78 of a tune called "Let Me Off Uptown." Roy sang and played-on that.
Uh-huh. I have that one too. 78.
And, of course, his the script was "After You've Gone." Remember that introduction? Tuh-duh-duh-duh, tuh-duh-duh-duh --
That was something. He did, he played that in my band, even before Krupa. This was the thing Roy did best, you know. Had the chops.
